messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 29
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Painter
  trauma_type: Mugging or robbery
  pcl5: 49

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Dream Residue: Waking up from a nightmare, Spatial Triggers: Physical locations, Intrusive Memory: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly
  Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively, Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger, Scanning for Danger: I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
  Memory: Incomplete Picture: I feel like I am only remembering parts of what happened and the rest is missing, Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt, Hard to Recall Deliberately: When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
  Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted, Isolation: I feel isolated and set apart from others, Can't Rely on Others: I can't rely on other people

Vignette:
Sandeep, a 29-year-old South Asian man married to Priya, has been struggling with recurrent nightmares and triggers that date back to his traumatic experience of being mugged. Sandeep works as a painter, often working on large commercial projects where he spends long hours outside in the city streets. The incident occurred one evening when Sandeep was returning home from work through an alleyway near downtown. He was suddenly confronted by two masked men who demanded his wallet and phone at gunpoint. In the struggle that ensued, one of the assailants pushed him to the ground, leaving him feeling helpless and vulnerable. Since then, Sandeep has found himself waking up frequently in a cold sweat, his heart racing from vivid nightmares of the mugging. Sandeep's triggers are potent reminders of the trauma he experienced. The alleyway where it happened is now a spatial trigger that he actively avoids. He often wakes up disoriented and scared, still feeling the intense fear from his dreams. These nightmares have left him irritable and quick to anger, especially in crowded or unfamiliar places where he constantly scans for signs of danger. His body feels perpetually tense, as if always on high alert. The memory of the event itself is fragmented; Sandeep struggles with recalling specific details deliberately but finds himself unexpectedly flooded with memories when triggered by locations that resemble the scene of the mugging. These intrusive memories are accompanied by intense guilt, a sense that he should have done something differently to prevent the attack. When he tries to recall the event consciously, he finds it difficult and feels like parts of what happened remain missing. Sandeep's negative appraisals about his experiences have become deeply ingrained. He has come to believe that people can't be trusted and feels increasingly isolated from others. This mistrust extends to Priya as well; even though she is supportive, Sandeep struggles to rely on her for emotional support because he fears it might not be enough if another threat emerges. At work, Sandeep’s avoidance behaviors have begun to affect his job performance. He often declines jobs that require him to work in areas where he feels vulnerable or unsafe. This has led to strained relationships with his colleagues who don’t understand his reluctance and perceive it as a lack of commitment. Despite these challenges, the most significant impact is on his relationship with Priya, who senses his growing distance but doesn't fully comprehend the extent of his trauma. Sandeep finally sought help because he realized that his irritability was affecting both his work and his marriage. He fears becoming a person who can’t trust or rely on others, losing the connection to Priya and feeling perpetually isolated. In therapy, Sandeep is hopeful for strategies to manage his symptoms better, regain control over his daily life, and reconnect with those he cares about most. Through this process, Sandeep hopes to find ways to mitigate the constant tension and threat monitoring that dominate his day-to-day experiences. He wants to reclaim a sense of safety and trust in himself and others, ultimately striving for a more balanced and fulfilling life.
